internal.title: Incident Report: High Kafka Consumer Lag in Accounting Service
internal.body:
At 10:11 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for high Kafka consumer lag in the accounting service. The lag reached approximately 5200 records, accompanied by increased p95 latency of 0.25 seconds, indicating processing delays. Initial diagnosis rounds confirmed latency issues but attempts to mitigate via service restart or scaling were blocked by deployment guardrails due to missing dry run validations and rollback constraints.

CPU utilization was moderate at 25%, and memory metrics were unavailable due to budget limits. Error rates remained low at 0.2%, with no error logs or traces found, making error injection an unlikely cause.

The incident was escalated for further investigation and resolution. The root cause remains under analysis as mitigation actions were constrained by deployment policies.

Timeline highlights:
- 10:11 Alert received
- 10:30 Diagnosis rounds initiated
- Multiple mitigation proposals refused due to guardrail policies
- Incident escalated for further handling

Next steps include reviewing deployment policies to enable more flexible mitigation options and continued monitoring of the accounting service latency and consumer lag.

external.body: Between 10:11 and shortly thereafter on 2026-11-08, the accounting service experienced intermittent processing delays resulting in increased message processing times. This caused a temporary backlog in message consumption from our data streams. Our engineering team identified the issue and is actively working to resolve it. We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused and appreciate your patience as we improve service reliability.
